title: This week's learning objectives
html:
This week’s question: does it matter where you help?

Most people choose where to give or volunteer by what feels close or urgent. This week makes the case that the choice matters much more than that. Some ways of helping do tens or hundreds of times more good than others, and the people who could benefit count equally wherever they live.

That is also why the first skill is reasoning transparency. If the differences are that large, being wrong is costly. The fastest way to find out you are wrong is to let other people see how you reached your view.

By the end of this week, you will be able to:

  • Explain what effective altruism is and the argument for it

  • Explain why impartiality and cost-effectiveness matter when deciding where to help

  • Make your own reasoning transparent, and assess the transparency of an argument you read

Time commitment

  • Reading: about 65 minutes (course text, one introduction to effective altruism, two chapters of Singer, Ord’s essay)

  • Quiz: about 5 minutes

  • Exercises: about 35 minutes

  • Total before the session: about 1 hour 45 minutes
